title: Hosted API session gap-wave retrospective and runbook (draft)
content:
Executive summary:

On 2029-06-18 between ~15:22 and 15:43 UTC we observed a P0 outage pattern we are calling a "session gap-wave": transient waves of streaming session gaps and short 5xx spikes across multiple host pools in us-west-2 that resulted in a ~7% reduction in overall streaming throughput and elevated p95/p99 tail latency for the Hosted API. Customer-facing impact: several enterprise customers saw aborted streaming responses and a higher rate of reconnect attempts; any request using long-lived streaming with KV cache reuse experienced partial output loss and increased client retries.

Detect & notify:
- First alert: internal streaming-signal-loss SLI breached at 15:22 UTC (automation threshold: >3.5% session gap rate for 1m).
- PagerDuty triggered PD-INC-13762; on-call SREs paged and triaged.
- Automated circuit-breaker temporarily reduced ingress to affected host pools at 15:27 UTC.

Impact summary:
- Duration: ~21 minutes (15:22 - 15:43 UTC); client reconnects and retries persisted longer for some flows but core surge resolved.
- Scope: ~12% of streaming connections in us-west-2 observed at least one gap event; global effects limited due to routing fallbacks.
- Severity: P0 (service availability degradation affecting customer SLAs for streaming).
- Downstream: two customers reported degraded user experiences; no data loss reported in persisted artifacts, but in-flight streaming fragments were dropped and retransmitted by clients.

Timeline (condensed):
- 15:18 UTC - pre-incident: a short internal canary job that exercises long-streams completed; no failures logged.
- 15:21 UTC - gradual rise in ephemeral-lease-renewal error rate on edge gateways (auth errors surfaced in logs, correlated with short time windows).
- 15:22 UTC - streaming-signal-loss SLI crossed automation threshold -> first alert and PD page.
- 15:24 UTC - SREs notice KV cache eviction pressure on several model-serving shards; correlates with higher-than-normal prefix cache misses.
- 15:26 UTC - control-plane observed a flurry of session rebind attempts; rebalancer started moving ~3% of sessions between shards.
- 15:27 UTC - adaptive ingress throttle engaged for affected host pool; synthetic traffic shows partial recovery for short requests but streaming remains degraded.
- 15:33 UTC - rollback of a recent edge auth token change in staging (suspected contributor) completed; reduced auth error rates on gateways.
- 15:39 UTC - KV lease manager tuning change rolled forward (short-term mitigation) to reduce evictions; observed decline in cache miss rate.
- 15:43 UTC - alert conditions cleared; streaming SLI returned to baseline after~10m stabilization window.

Root cause analysis (high level):
Primary root cause: an unexpected interaction between edge gateway token renewal throttling and the KV cache lease manager caused a cascade that amplified session churn and produced bursts of in-flight session rebinds. Specifically:
- Edge gateways started returning transient auth errors (403-like) under a short-lived control-plane token refresh overload. This caused clients to tear down some long-lived streaming sessions and reconnect.
- The reconnects created hot prefixes and concentrated KV cache pressure on a subset of model-serving shards. Our lease-based KV cache eviction policy reacted by aggressively evicting entries in those shards to reclaim memory and allow new KV allocations.
- Eviction caused higher tokenization and model re-warm costs for reconnecting sessions which increased CPU pressure and increased latency for fragment assembly. That latency caused additional client-side timeouts and reconnect behavior, producing a positive feedback loop — the "gap-wave".

Contributing factors:
- Recent small control-plane change (token refresh batching) increased token refresh latency by ~120ms at the edge under burst conditions; the change was rolled back in staging but had a partial rollout in production.
- KV lease eviction heuristic was tuned for aggressive recovery under memory pressure; it lacked a short-circuit for bursty reconnect patterns (no rate-limiter for evictions against a shard experiencing high new-writes).
- No early-warning metric correlated token-refresh latency to session churn; the SLO deck had separate alerts for auth and for streaming gaps but not an integrated composite.
- The session rebalancer aggressively moved sessions when lease metadata showed skewed ownership; the movement amplified transient cache misses.

Immediate mitigations taken during incident:
- >15:27 UTC: adaptive ingress throttle engaged automatically and was extended by SREs to reduce new session acceptance for affected pools; this lowered inbound reconnection rate and gave caches time to stabilize.
- 15:33 UTC: control-plane rollback of partial token-refresh rollout in production edge (stop the mitigation causing auth errors).
- 15:39 UTC: applied temporary softening to KV lease eviction (raise eviction threshold & add temporary per-shard eviction rate limit).
- 15:41 UTC: adjusted rebalancer cooldown to avoid moving sessions for 60s after an ownership change, preventing bounce during stabilization.

Why mitigations worked:
- Reducing reconnection load disrupted the positive feedback loop and allowed caches to refill and CPU pressure to drop.
- Rolling back token-refresh change removed the auth error source so clients stopped unnecessary reconnects.
- Throttling evictions prevented cascaded cache thrashing while rebalancer cooldown avoided amplifying the instability.

Long-term remediation plan (proposed):
(1) Observability & alerts
  - Create composite alarm that correlates edge token-refresh latency, session-creation rate, and KV cache eviction rate to detect early gap-wave formation (owner: Lena; due: 2029-07-05).
  - Add a synthetic long-stream test that mimics production prefix distributions and runs in us-west-2 every 5m; fail and alert on >1% gap events (owner: Marcus; due: 2029-06-30).

(2) Control plane & edge
  - Harden token refresh path: add backpressure/queue length controls and circuit-breaker for refresh batching (owner: Priya; due: 2029-07-12).

(3) KV cache & lease manager
  - Implement per-shard eviction rate-limiter and a burst-aware eviction policy that pauses eviction when session-creation rate spikes above baseline (owner: Eng-Serving/Cache team; due: 2029-07-26).
  - Add a lightweight cache-warm path for reconnecting sessions to avoid full model rewarm on every reconnect (owner: Marcus; due: 2029-08-09).

(4) Session rebalancer & routing
  - Change rebalancer decision logic to consider recent eviction activity and short-lived ownership churn; conservative mode for 60s after significant join/leave (owner: Eng-Serving/Router; due: 2029-07-19).
  - Add a canary gating for rebalancer aggressiveness changes with a fast rollback path (owner: Platform Eng; due: 2029-08-01).

(5) Runbook improvements (this doc)
  - Publish a dedicated "gap-wave" runbook with detection thresholds, immediate mitigations, and post-incident checklist (owner: Aisha; due: 2029-06-28).

Action items (short list with owners & deadlines):
- Aisha: Finalize and publish runbook draft into Confluence; include play-by-play run commands and safe rollback steps (due 2029-06-28).
- Lena: Implement composite alarm + dashboard (due 2029-07-05).
- Priya: Fix token refresh backpressure and add circuit-breaker; add deployment gating (due 2029-07-12).
- Marcus: Deliver synthetic long-stream test harness + runbook integration (due 2029-06-30).
- Eng-Serving/Cache: Implement per-shard eviction rate-limiter (MVP) and submit design doc (due 2029-07-15).

Draft runbook (playbook) - high level steps to run during recurrence:
1) Detection
  - Check streaming-signal-loss SLI and session-creation rate for target region.
  - Query edge token-refresh latency graph and auth error rate (403/401 spike).
  - Check KV eviction rate by shard and sharded memory pressure metrics.
2) Triage
  - If token-refresh latency > 50ms over baseline and auth errors present, escalate to control-plane on-call immediately.
  - If reconnects are spiking, enable adaptive ingress throttle for the affected host pool (safe default: reduce new sessions by 30%).
3) Short-term mitigations (safe order)
  - Engage ingress throttle (automated can be overridden in Console).
  - Apply temporary per-shard eviction softening (increase thresholds).
  - Increase rebalancer cooldown to stop moves for 60s on affected shards.
  - Coordinate with Control Plane: inspect token-refresh rollout and consider rollback.
4) Validation
  - Observe streaming gap SLI and cache miss rate for improvement over 3m windows.
  - Confirm clients stop reconnect storm and edge auth errors return to baseline.
5) Communication
  - Post to #sre-incident with concise status updates every 10 minutes while in P0.
  - If customers affected, coordinate PM/CS for targeted communications.
6) Post-incident
  - Run the postmortem template, assign owners, and schedule follow-up review within 5 business days.

Open questions raised by the incident:
- Why did the token-refresh partial rollout reach prod gates despite staging rollback? Gap in deployment gating/fast rollback path needs investigation (owner: Platform Eng).
- Can the KV eviction policy be made predictive (based on prefix/hotspot detection) rather than reactive to memory signals? (owner: Eng-Serving/Cache).
- Are there client-side reconnection behaviors we should document and recommend (e.g., exponential backoff tuning) to reduce bounce amplification? (owner: Developer Experience).

Appendix: useful queries & commands (examples)
- kql: sum(rate(streaming_gap_events[1m])) by region,hostpool
- grafana: edge.token_refresh.latency p95 (filter: us-west-2)
- admin: enable-ingress-throttle --pool=usw2-pool-4 --percent=30 --reason="session-gap-wave"

Notes & context (informal):
- This feels like a classic feedback-loop where control-plane latency + cache pressure + aggressive repair (rebalancer) combine to create emergent instability. That makes it hard to reproduce in unit tests — synthetic long-streams that match production prefix skew are going to be key.
- Avoid large-scope immediate code changes; prefer short-term config mitigations + rollout gating while we design the eviction policy changes.

Draft status: this is a working doc for SRE review. Please add suggestions inline and assign owners in the action-items table above.

-- Aisha Kapoor & on-call SREs
